case_name: Dr. Ms. O.Z. Hussain v Union Of India And Ors.
facts: This is an application u/art. 32 of the Constitution and the President of the National Council of Bio-Medical Scientists is the petitioner.
The reliefs asked for are on the allegation that the Group 'A' scientists of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare who are the members of the Council, are being discriminatingly treated;

Similar scientists in other Ministries, such as Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Environment and Ministry of Oceanography are recruited in terms of rules made under the proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution
It has been alleged that though several demands were pressed by the representatives of the Council, only a few were considered and yet there was no follow-up action for their implementation.
Annexure P-1 indicates the institutions located in different parts of the country where the posts of 'A' Group scientists who are members of the Council work.
The petitioner has placed on record the rules framed in exercise of powers under proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution in the Ministry of Science and Technology, covering Group 'A' scientists.
Rule 13 thereof provides avenues for promotion.

It has been pointed out therein that while there is a difference in the pay-scale in the establishment of Director General of Health Services, there is no disparity in respect of similar posts in the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) or in the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi or the Post--Graduate Institute at Chandigarh.
The 4th Pay Commission in Chapter 29, paragraph 29.8 recommended: 'The question of granting incentive to officers and staff who acquire higher qualification has also engaged our attention.'
Office Memorandum in the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension indicated that this recommendation of the Pay Commission has been accepted by the Government.
In fact, at the hearing of the writ petition, respondent's counsel found it difficult to support the prevailing position.

We are of the opinion that these four kinds of allowances, which are admissible to the medical doctors are also admissible to the Group 'A' scientists under the non-medical category employed in the establishment of Director General of Health Services.
issues: What is the justification for the disparity in the scale of pay between the two categories of officers?

Why do similarly placed officers in other Ministries have the benefit of promotion, while the non-medical 'A' Group scientists in the establishment of Director General of Health Services would be deprived of such advantage?
What are the promotional avenues available to Group 'A' scientists in other Ministries, and why are they not available to these scientists in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare?
Is there any justification for denying nonpractising allowance to the Group 'A' scientists in the non-medical category?
What is the obligation of the Ministry of Health to attend to the representations of the Council and its members and provide promotional avenue for this category of officers?
petitioner_arguments: The Group 'A' scientists are being discriminatingly treated;

There is no justification why while similarly placed officers in other Ministries would have the benefit of promotion, the non-medical 'A' Group scientists in the establishment of Director General of Health Services would be deprived of such advantage.

In a welfare State, it is necessary that there should be an efficient public service and, therefore, it should have been the obligation of the Ministry of Health to attend to the representations of the Council and its members and provide promotional avenue for this category of officers.
respondent_arguments: The qualifications of officers in the two wings are different and the difference in the pay scales has always existed.

There is no justification why similarly placed officers in other Ministries would have the benefit of promotion, while the non-medical 'A' Group scientists in the establishment of Director General of Health Services would be deprived of such advantage.
court_reasoning: The provision for promotion increases efficiency of the public service while stagnation reduces efficiency and makes the service ineffective.
Promotion is thus a normal incidence of service.

There too is no justification why while similarly placed officers in other Ministries would have the benefit of promotion, the non-medical 'A' Group scientists in the establishment of Director General of Health Services would be deprived of such advantage.
holding: The Writ Petition is allowed and the following directions are issued:

(1) Within four months from today, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of the Union of India shall frame a set of appropriate rules, inter alia, providing suitable promotional avenue for the 'A' Group scientists in the non-medical wing of the establishment of Director General of Health Services;

(2) These 'A' Group scientists shall be entitled to book allowance, higher degree allowance, risk allowance and conveyance allowance at the same rate as is admissible to doctors in the medical wing in the Directorate w.e.f. 1.4.1989;
(3) Government shall examine the tenability of the claim of equal pay scales for this category of officers within four months from today.
cases_cited: Dr. Ms. O.Z. Hussain v Union Of India
